notes: Rules the compatibility engine (spec 05) enforces. Each rule has a machine-readable 'check' (types defined in spec 02, section 8) so code never hard-codes the logic, and a 'failure' the learner sees when a pairing is blocked or degrades. Paths point at resolved device instances (the size the learner picked). Questionnaire 3.4 and 3.12: anything not allowed is blocked, with its reason. Roles in 'pair' map to device kinds through 'roles'. When a path resolves to an options list, comparisons use the selected value unless the check names an aggregate ('leftAgg' or 'rightAgg': 'max' or 'min'), which capability lists such as wireCompatibility use.

rules.text: A 0.035 in wire needs an 18-gauge or larger needle; a 0.018 in wire needs a 22-gauge or larger needle.

failure.message: This wire will not pass through this needle.

rules.text: A catheter's lumen must be rated for the wire (most diagnostic catheters take 0.035 or 0.038 in).

failure.message: This wire is too large for this catheter's lumen.

rules.note: Catheter labels state the largest compatible wire.

rules.text: A microcatheter's inner diameter must exceed the microwire's diameter.

failure.message: This wire is too large for the microcatheter.

rules.note: Inner diameters per model in microcatheters.json.

rules.text: Sheath French size is its inner diameter and catheter French size is its outer diameter, so a 5F catheter fits a 5F sheath.

failure.message: This catheter will not enter the sheath valve.

rules.text: The parent catheter's inner diameter must exceed the microcatheter's proximal outer diameter.

failure.message: The microcatheter will not fit through this catheter.

rules.note: Tapered microcatheters are larger at the hub than at the tip. A near-equal fit should raise friction (spec 04).

rules.text: The coil's delivery platform (0.016, 0.018, 0.020 in for Ruby, or 0.035 in) must be within the catheter's coil limit.

failure.message: The coil jams; the catheter must be replaced.

rules.note: Ruby is a 0.020 in coil platform that needs a high-flow 0.025 in lumen such as Lantern (penumbra-platform-2023); Maestro coil limits from merit-maestro.

rules.text: Particle size must be within the catheter's stated maximum (400 to 1,000 um by model).

failure.message: Injection resistance rises, then the catheter clogs.

rules.text: AVP 4 goes through a 0.038 in-compatible diagnostic catheter; MVP-3Q and 5Q through a microcatheter.

failure.message: This plug will not deliver through this catheter.

rules.text: DMSO-based agents (Onyx) go only through DMSO-compatible catheters.
Flush the catheter with dextrose before glue; saline or blood in the lumen sets it.

failure.message: Flush with dextrose first, or the glue will set in the lumen.

rules.text: Power-injector pressure must stay at or below the catheter's rating (microcatheters 300 to 1,200 psi).
Wire length must exceed the catheter's length plus the distance to the target plus a hand-hold margin; exchanges need 180 to 300 cm wires.

failure.message: The wire is too short: you will lose wire position during the exchange.

rules.text: Pelvic work from the radial artery needs 125 cm catheters and 150 cm microcatheters.

failure.message: This catheter is too short to reach the pelvis from the wrist.

rules.text: A balloon or stent needs its labeled wire platform and sheath (for example 0.018 in balloons through 4 to 5F).

failure.message: The device will not track on this wire or will not enter the sheath.

rules.text: Angio-Seal uses a 6 or 8F device sheath; Mynx is for sheaths up to 7F; above 8F, pre-close with two Perclose devices.

failure.message: Bleeding: this device does not close a sheath this size.

rules.text: Catheters advance in the vessel only over a wire.

failure.message: Lead with the wire before advancing the catheter.
